C9000025.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 025 (Short Egyptian fractions.; papers: Short Egyptian fractions; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/025.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C_DIVISOR_MOMENT_REAL.statement: For every fixed real D,r >= 1, the full shifted truncated-divisor r-th moment in build/divisors.tex::lem:divisor holds eventually in S, uniformly in the stated real X,Y and natural N.

C_DIVISOR_MOMENT_NAT.statement: The upstream uniform_divisor_moment natural-exponent theorem and all of its non-Mathlib proof dependencies compile without holes under Lean 4.31.0.

C_DIVISOR_MOMENT_BRIDGE.statement: The natural-exponent theorem implies the manuscript's real-exponent theorem using an integer ceiling, X=exp(log X), the shifted-sum bijection, and exact natural-floor endpoints.

C_GROWING_DIVISOR_THRESHOLD.statement: A single S0(D) supports all real moments up to log(S)/(200000 log(log(S))); an infinite primorial family fails at every fixed C>1/2 times log(S)/log(log(S)).

C_GROWING_DIVISOR_UPPER.statement: The universal real-order upper theorem with c=1/200000, the original right-hand side, and the full manuscript shift range.

C_GROWING_DIVISOR_OBSTRUCTION.statement: For t=2^m, S=2t, N=product_{p<=t}p-1, X=exp(S/(2log S)), Y=sqrt X, every fixed C>1/2 eventually violates the moment bound at r=C log(S)/log(log(S)).

C_GROWING_DIVISOR_NOVELTY.statement: Publishable significance and novelty of the paired growing-moment result remain to be established against applicable primary literature.

C_GROWING_DIVISOR_COMPARISON.statement: The retrieved Nair--Tenenbaum and Henriot theorems retain fixed growth-class and positive-power interval parameter dependencies and do not directly assert the target growing-order uniformity.
